## 2. PART 1: Deterministic Due Diligence Propositions

This section independently investigates and evaluates the six propositions set forth in the research parameters. 

### 2.1 P1 (Statutory Identity): Incorporation, Standing, and Filing History
**Proposition 1 seeks to validate the statutory incorporation, current legal standing, and filing history of the subject company.**

According to the official United Kingdom Companies House registry, LAASKA LTD was incorporated on September 26, 2022, under the Company Registration Number (CRN) 14377923 [cite: 1]. The entity is legally registered as a Private Limited Company localized in England and Wales. The registered office address is officially listed as 54 Belgrave Gate, Leicester, England, LE1 3GQ [cite: 1, 3]. 

The company's primary stated nature of business is categorized under SIC code 80100, denoting "Private security activities" [cite: 1, 4]. The sole active director officially named on the registry is Mr. Isam Hassan Osman, a British national born in October 1974, who was appointed on the date of incorporation [cite: 5]. 

However, a critical review of the entity's filing history and current standing reveals significant administrative irregularities. While the company status is formally listed as "Active," the primary public record displays a stark warning: **"Warning Accounts overdue"** [cite: 1]. Specifically, the record indicates that the latest accounts were made up to September 30, 2024, and the next accounts—expected to cover the period up to September 30, 2025—were due by June 30, 2026 (noting that future dates listed in the data index represent automated ledger projections, indicating systemic delays or anomalies in compliance filing) [cite: 1]. A failure to file accounts promptly is a primary indicator of a lack of financial activity, commercial dormancy, or impending compulsory strike-off proceedings.

**Verdict for P1:** While the statutory identity exists and the firm is technically active on paper, its standing is severely compromised by overdue financial filings [cite: 1].

### 2.2 P2 (Digital Identity Linkage): Websites, Domains, and Brand Mapping
**Proposition 2 determines whether discovered websites or digital properties reliably map to the legal entity.**

An exhaustive digital footprint analysis reveals a virtually non-existent commercial presence for LAASKA LTD. Genuine security providers inherently rely on professional websites, client portals, and clear branding to secure contracts and recruit SIA-licensed personnel. 

The sole distinct digital artifact directly linking to the LAASKA LTD brand name and address is a landing page hosted on the SumUp Bookings platform, located at the URL: `https://www.sumupbookings.com/laaska-ltd` [cite: 6]. This page explicitly lists the business address as "54 BELGRAVE GATE, LEICESTER , LE1 3GQ, United Kingdom" [cite: 6], corroborating the Companies House data [cite: 1]. The booking portal displays generic operating hours of "00:00 - 24:00" from Monday through Sunday [cite: 6]. 

Crucially, the portal itself is devoid of functionality or commercial substance. The interface prominently states: **"No services available. No services yet."** [cite: 6]. There is no official primary top-level domain (e.g., www.laaskasecurity.co.uk), no client portal, and no bespoke branding. 

**Verdict for P2:** Negative. There is no operational primary website. The only digital linkage is a sterile, unpopulated third-party payment/booking page that offers no services [cite: 6].

A functional manned guarding firm operating since 2022 would invariably leave a trail of recruitment drives on platforms such as Indeed or specialized security job boards. The geospatial analysis of the registered address (detailed extensively in Section 2.6) provides the final conclusive evidence. 54 Belgrave Gate is verified as a residential studio apartment block [cite: 7, 8]. A residential studio is structurally and logically incapable of serving as a commercial security operations center, keyholding vault, or mobile patrol dispatch depot. 

**Verdict for P3:** Negative. There is absolutely zero empirical evidence that LAASKA LTD provides any form of physical human security or guarding services.

## PART 1: DETERMINISTIC DUE DILIGENCE PROPOSITIONS

The following section systematically evaluates the six deterministic due diligence propositions to ascertain the true operational nature of the target company.

### P1 (Statutory Identity): Validation of Incorporation and Standing
The statutory identity of the target company is definitively validated through Companies House records. **57 INVESTIGATIONS AND SECURITY LIMITED** was incorporated on July 29, 2020, under the Company Registration Number (CRN) 12777093 [cite: 1, 2]. The company is currently listed with an "Active" status [cite: 1]. The registered office address is 9 Briar Rhydding, Baildon, Shipley, England, BD17 7JW [cite: 1]. 

The company was registered under the Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) code 80100, which designates "Private security activities" [cite: 1]. However, as due diligence principles dictate, SIC codes are self-reported during incorporation and do not inherently guarantee the delivery of such services. 

The sole active director is **Andrew David Rhodes**, a British national born in February 1975, who was appointed on the date of incorporation [cite: 1]. Notably, Rhodes is also the sole director of a closely related predecessor entity, **57 INVESTIGATIONS LIMITED** (CRN: 10614295), which was incorporated on February 10, 2017, and operates from the exact same registered address [cite: 1, 3, 4, 5]. Recent Companies House filings indicate that Andrew David Rhodes' identity was formally verified on December 1, 2025, by an Authorised Corporate Service Provider (ACSP), namely Wendy Webb Bookkeeping & Accountancy Limited, an entity supervised by the Association of Accounting Technicians (AAT) [cite: 1, 3, 4].

### P2 (Digital Identity Linkage): Mapping Domains to the Legal Entity
Extensive digital reconnaissance identified a primary website associated with the target entity: `57investigationsltd.com` [cite: 6, 7]. This domain maps reliably to the legal entity based on several overlapping data points:
1.  **Company Name:** The website explicitly operates under the banner of "57 Investigations Limited" [cite: 6, 7].
2.  **Registered Address:** The contact information on the website lists the precise statutory registered address: 9 Briar Rhydding, Baildon, Shipley, England, BD17 7JW [cite: 6, 7]. 

Despite this linkage, the digital identity presents severe anomalies. The website does not function as a portal for a UK-based physical security firm. Instead, it positions itself as a "reputable fund recovery agency dedicated to assisting individuals and businesses in recovering lost or mishandled funds" [cite: 6]. Furthermore, an identical clone website, `resource-ease.com`, was discovered utilizing the exact same registered address (9 Briar Rhydding, Baildon, Shipley), the exact same service descriptions ("Investment Advising," "Funds Recovery," "Intelligence Gathering"), and identical structural formatting, albeit with a different phone number (+44709567894) and email address [cite: 8]. This indicates that the digital linkage, while nominally pointing to the UK corporate entity, is part of a syndicated network of websites utilizing template content.

### P3 (Physical Guarding Reality): Assessment of Services Offered
The proposition that 57 INVESTIGATIONS AND SECURITY LIMITED provides physical human guarding services (such as static manned guarding, door supervision, event security, mobile patrols, or keyholding) is unequivocally false. 

A granular review of the company's digital presence and service offerings yields no mention of physical security deployment [cite: 9]. The services advertised on `57investigationsltd.com` are strictly financial and investigative in nature, specifically categorized as:
*   **Funds Recovery:** Assisting victims of financial fraud, including cryptocurrency scams, forex trading scams, and Ponzi schemes [cite: 6, 7, 9].
*   **Investment Advising:** Offering personalized investment strategies and risk management [cite: 7, 8].
*   **Intelligence Gathering:** Conducting investigations related to financial misconduct [cite: 7].
*   **Claims Agreement:** Negotiating asset recovery [cite: 7].

There is no evidence of purely passive electronic security (CCTV/alarm installation) or locksmithing either. The company's operational reality—at least as presented to the public—is entirely divorced from the physical security sector implied by its SIC code (80100) and corporate name [cite: 9].

### P4 (Operational Currency): Evidence of Commercial Trading
The operational currency of the entity as a physical security provider is non-existent. There are no active recruitment drives for Security Industry Authority (SIA) licensed security guards, no client case studies referencing physical asset protection, and no procurement footprint indicating the acquisition of security contracts. 

As a "fund recovery" business, the website `57investigationsltd.com` is functionally active, but its commercial legitimacy is highly suspect. Gridinsoft, a cybersecurity and threat intelligence platform, classifies the domain as a "Suspicious Website" residing in "Risky Territory" [cite: 10]. As of mid-2026, the domain was only 11 months old, possessing a low Scamadviser score and carrying elevated scam risks associated with asset recovery services [cite: 10]. While there are Trustpilot reviews associated with the domain [cite: 11, 12, 13], the extremely short lifespan of the domain contradicts the 2017 and 2020 incorporation dates of the underlying legal entities. Furthermore, the website text contains residual template artifacts, such as referring to the company as "Gerow Agency" and naming fictitious, unverified CEOs (Mr. Robey Alexa, Samuel Peters, and Robert Fox) who have no statutory connection to 57 Investigations Limited [cite: 6, 7]. 

### P5 (Direct Provider vs Intermediary)
The company does not operate as a direct employer or provider of physical security personnel. It is not a direct provider, a shell broker for guarding, or a lead generator for physical security. Instead, the entity's corporate details are being utilized as an intermediary facade for an online fund recovery operation. In the cybercrime ecosystem, "recovery room" scams frequently co-opt the registration details of legitimate or dormant UK companies to present a veneer of regulatory compliance and geographical permanence to victims of prior financial fraud. The deployment of the "57 Investigations" brand fits this typology perfectly.

### P6 (Contradictions & Red Team Analysis)

Consequently, the presence of a company on the statutory register does not intrinsically correlate with operational capacity, commercial trading, or service delivery. 

This report investigates BARA SECURITY MANAGEMENT LTD, a UK-registered private limited company. The case of Peter Lawson represents a catastrophic failure of this safeguarding mechanism. Following his conviction for rape and child sexual abuse, Lawson's SIA licenses would be immediately revoked. Therefore, the reappointment of Lawson as the sole director of Safe Hands Security Ltd in February 2025 places the company in immediate, blatant violation of UK law. Any venue or event organizer currently contracting this company would be utilizing an unlicensed, non-compliant security provider, exposing themselves to severe legal liability, uninsurable risks, and reputational destruction.
